# Four-Week Coding Interview Prep in JavaScript — Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This four-week intensive course is designed to prepare intermediate JavaScript developers for technical coding interviews at major tech companies and startups. The curriculum balances **algorithmic problem-solving**, **JavaScript-specific patterns**, and **data structure mastery** with practical, time-constrained coding challenges.

**Who this is for:**
- Developers with 1–3 years of JavaScript experience seeking to strengthen interview skills
- Career changers transitioning into software engineering roles
- Engineers moving between companies or seniority levels

**Why it matters:**
Technical interviews heavily emphasize algorithm optimization, clean code patterns, and the ability to articulate your reasoning under pressure. This course bridges the gap between day-to-day development and interview-ready problem-solving, covering the 80/20 of what actually appears in interviews.

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Array and String Manipulation** — sorting, searching, slicing, frequency maps, sliding window techniques
- **Linked Lists & Pointer Manipulation** — traversal, reversal, cycle detection, partition operations
- **Trees & Graphs** — DFS/BFS, binary search trees, level-order traversal, connected components
- **Dynamic Programming** — memoization, tabulation, overlapping subproblems, classic patterns (coin change, longest subsequence)
- **Hash Maps & Sets** — collision handling, frequency counting, two-pointer techniques, cache design
- **Recursion & Backtracking** — tree/permutation generation, constraint satisfaction, pruning strategies
- **Stack & Queue Applications** — parentheses matching, monotonic stacks, BFS with queues
- **Sorting & Searching Algorithms** — merge sort, quicksort, binary search, heap operations

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Week 1: Foundations & Arrays (Days 1–7)**

**Days 1–2: Core Data Structures Review**
- Refresh arrays, objects, sets, maps in JavaScript
- Understand time/space complexity notation (Big O)
- Complete 8–10 warm-up problems: two-sum variants, array reversal, duplicate removal

**Days 3–4: Array Techniques**
- Sliding window pattern (max subarray sum, longest substring without repeating)
- Two-pointer approach (sorted pair finding, container with most water)
- Prefix sums and cumulative frequency
- Complete 12–14 problems

**Days 5–6: String Manipulation**
- String reversal, palindrome checking, anagram detection
- Pattern matching, character frequency
- String compression, word rotation
- Complete 10–12 problems

**Day 7: Review & Timed Practice**
- Retake 5–6 problems from the week under timed conditions (25–45 min per problem)
- Document lessons learned; identify weak patterns

**Week 1 Target: 30–35 practice tasks**

---

### **Week 2: Complex Data Structures (Days 8–14)**

**Days 8–9: Linked Lists**
- Node structure, traversal, and reversal
- Cycle detection (Floyd's algorithm)
- Merge sorted lists, remove duplicates
- Complete 8–10 problems

**Days 10–11: Trees & Graphs Basics**
- Binary tree traversal (in-order, pre-order, post-order, level-order)
- Binary search tree validation and insertion
- Graph representations (adjacency list, matrix)
- DFS and BFS implementations
- Complete 12–14 problems

**Days 12–13: Advanced Tree Operations**
- Lowest common ancestor, path sum, diameter
- Serialize/deserialize trees
- Tree reconstruction from traversals
- Complete 10–12 problems

**Day 14: Timed Mixed Problems**
- Combine linked list, tree, and graph problems under time pressure
- Target: 1 problem every 35–40 minutes

**Week 2 Target: 40–45 practice tasks**

---

### **Week 3: Algorithms & Dynamic Programming (Days 15–21)**

**Days 15–16: Sorting & Searching**
- Merge sort, quicksort implementation
- Binary search variants (leftmost, rightmost, rotated array)
- Counting sort for constrained inputs
- Complete 8–10 problems

**Days 17–18: Recursion & Backtracking**
- Permutations, combinations, subsets generation
- N-Queens, Sudoku solver, letter combinations
- Pruning strategies
- Complete 10–12 problems

**Days 19–20: Dynamic Programming Fundamentals**
- Fibonacci and climbing stairs (memoization vs. tabulation)
- Coin change problem (unbounded knapsack)
- Longest increasing subsequence, edit distance
- Complete 12–14 problems

**Day 21: Algorithm Synthesis**
- Mixed algorithm challenges combining multiple techniques
- Optimize previous DP solutions for space and time

**Week 3 Target: 40–45 practice tasks**

---

### **Week 4: Integration & Interview Simulation (Days 22–28)**

**Days 22–23: Stack & Queue Specialized Problems**
- Monotonic stack (largest rectangle, daily temperatures)
- LRU cache design
- Parentheses matching, expression evaluation
- Complete 8–10 problems

**Days 24–25: Mixed Problem Marathon**
- Random selection from all previous topics
- 2–3 problems per day under strict time limits
- Complete 10–12 problems

**Days 26–27: Mock Interview Sessions**
- Simulate real interviews: 45–60 minutes for 2 problems
- Practice verbal communication and pseudo-code articulation
- Complete 4–6 full mock problems

**Day 28: Final Review & Weak Spots**
- Revisit any topics with <70% success rate
- Complete final 5–8 problems covering personal trouble areas

**Week 4 Target: 25–30 practice tasks**

**Total Over 4 Weeks: 98 practice tasks**

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Technical Problem-Solving**
- Rapidly identify which data structures and algorithms fit a problem
- Recognize problem patterns (e.g., "is this a DP problem?")
- Break complex problems into subproblems

### **Code Optimization**
- Refactor brute-force solutions toward O(n log n) or O(n)
- Understand space-time tradeoffs and make deliberate choices
- Write optimized JavaScript idioms (e.g., using Map over object for hash tables with non-string keys)

### **Clean Code Communication**
- Write readable, well-named variable code in under 10 minutes
- Explain your approach clearly before coding
- Test edge cases methodically

### **Interview-Specific JavaScript Patterns**
- Proper handling of `null`, `undefined`, and falsy values
- Efficient string/array manipulation (slice, splice, spread operator)
- Closure and scope in recursive functions
- Destructuring and modern syntax without sacrificing clarity

### **Time Management Under Pressure**
- Solve medium problems in 25–35 minutes consistently
- Hard problems in 40–50 minutes
- Leave 5–10 minutes for testing and edge case verification

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Type 1: Sliding Window / Two-Pointer**

**Problem:** Find the longest substring without repeating characters.

```javascript
/**
 * Approach: Sliding window with character frequency map
 * Time: O(n), Space: O(min(n, charset))
 */
function lengthOfLongestSubstring(s) {
  const charIndex = new Map();
  let maxLen = 0;
  let left = 0;

  for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++) {
    const char = s[right];
    
    // If character was seen in current window, move left pointer
    if (charIndex.has(char) && charIndex.get(char) >= left) {
      left = charIndex.get(char) + 1;
    }
    
    charIndex.set(char, right);
    maxLen = Math.max(maxLen, right - left + 1);
  }

  return maxLen;
}

// Test cases
console.log(lengthOfLongestSubstring("abcabcbb")); // 3 ("abc")
console.log(lengthOfLongestSubstring("bbbbb"));   // 1 ("b")
console.log(lengthOfLongestSubstring("pwwkew"));  // 3 ("wke")
```

**Key Interview Points:**
- Explain why sliding window works (monotonic property)
- Clarify when to move
